utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case IT-05-87/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Could I have the appearances for the parties, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Kyle Wood and Christine Dahl for the Prosecution, along with case manager Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Kyle Wood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And appearances for Appellant Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish good morning to all, Your Honours. I am co-counsel, Veljko Djurdjic. With me is Ms. Marie O'Leary, she is our legal assistant and a member of our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Before I proceed any further, I want to make sure that the Appellant Djordjevic is able to follow the proceedings in a language that he can understand. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So this Status Conference, as you know, is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis in its paragraph (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The idea is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the parties filed their Notices of Appeal, respectively on the 24th of May, 2011, and as you recall the first Status Conference was held and presided over by me on the 30th of May of this year. Today's Status Conference, being the second one, was scheduled by an order signed by me and issued on the 24th of August. Let's start with the first main issue; namely, the detention conditions and health of Appellant Djordjevic. First of all, I would like to point out particularly in relation to health issues, if there are any, that should appellant -- should your client, Mr. Djordjevic, wish so, we can discuss these in private session. So let me ask about -- inquire about the status of his detention conditions first. Are there any problems that your client would like to signal or raise or have discussed?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am co-counsel Veljko Djurdjic. As for the health and detention conditions, as regards my client, there have been no changes, and according to his words, everything is fine as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You have got nothing to add yourself, Mr. Djordjevic, have you? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I am fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the second matter that we are going to deal with is the recent procedural history and what arises in the wake of what has taken place already. On the 11th of March of this year, as you recall, the parties were granted an extension of time of 60 days to file their Notices of Appeal, this was mainly because of the complexity of the case which was recognised by myself and my colleagues in the Appeals Chamber. On the 24th of May, 2011, both the Prosecution and the Djordjevic Defence filed their respective Notices of Appeal. The Prosecution presented two grounds of appeal, while Djordjevic presented 19 grounds of appeal. On the 27th of May, 2011, the Djordjevic Defence filed a motion requesting an extension of time and word limit in respect of its appeal brief. At the Status Conference of a few days after, namely of the 30th of May, 2011, and after hearing oral submissions from the parties, I extended the dead-line for filing appeal briefs by seven days up to the 15th of August, 2011, and that was applicable for both parties. In addition, I granted the Djordjevic Defence team an extension of up to 15.000 words for its appeal brief. That brought up the total allowed of 4 to 5.000 words. I also granted the Prosecution the same extension in respect of its brief and response. Both appellants brief were filed on time on the 15th of August, and I wish here to thank you both for having been punctual in your filing. The respondent's briefs are due no longer than the 26th of September, namely, in another five days' time, and the briefs and reply no longer than the 11th of October, 2011. We need to move forward, and therefore I enjoin you to comply with these dead-lines to the best of your abilities. And I would also like to remind the parties, and this is very important what I am going to say, particularly in relation to the Defence, of the obligation to file public redacted versions of their confidential submissions. I note that the Prosecution filed already the public redacted version of its appeal brief on 17th August 2011. To date, however, more than a month later, we have not yet received a public redacted version of the Djordjevic appeal brief. I encourage the Defence to make this filing as soon as possible, and before I establish the date, I would like to know from you how long do you think it can take you or it would take you to be able to do this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would be able to do that after we received the respondent's brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but what does that have to do, because what I am asking for is a -- you filed a confidential appeal brief. Now you are required to also file a public redacted one; in other words, the brief itself is not going to change depending on what the respondent's brief will contain. So it's a question of going through what you have already filed confidentially and redact what needs to be redacted so that you can file it as a public redacted version of the same brief. So how long do you think -- this should have already been done, let's say, about a month ago. So when will you be in a position to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, because of the obligations we had we neglected this obligation, but we will do our best to submit and file this public redacted version as soon as next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So next week, 29th, all right. I will give you a little bit more than you have asked for. I will give you up to the 3rd of October, 3rd of October, to file the public redacted version. That means not the coming Monday, the Monday after. So you will have the rest of this week, entire next week, and Monday of the following week. Okay. Thank you. As regards the filing, I think I have got nothing else to say. We are expecting, as I said, the brief replies by not later than the 11th of October, and at this point I would like to ask you whether there are any issues that you have and that you would like to raise before we conclude. Start with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, just briefly, Your Honour. I noticed that you just said the 11th of October for the reply briefs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Earlier you had said the 10th of October. We just want to clarify. Our calculation also showed the 11th of October would be the due date for the reply briefs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If I said the 10th, I must have made a mistake somewhere. It's the 10th -- 11th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Any issues, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I do have an issue that I would like to raise, perhaps it's a bit too early, but we are getting closer to the time where the Defence would like to submit -- to file a request for an extension of the dead-line for the represent in brief, and also an extension -- another extension of the number of words in the appeals brief. We would request another 15.000 -- to be granted another 15.000 -- 1.500, which would mean that the total would amount to 6.000 words. Now the entire case has 65 pages with the annex -- the indictment, there are 14 municipalities mentioned in the indictment upon which our client was convicted, and also in the Appeals Chamber there -- in the appeal's brief there are 19 grounds of appeal mentioned by the Prosecutor. And you have allowed an extension to the Prosecutor as well to 45.000 words as -- which is the same number of words that you have granted us. So we believe that this extension would contribute to an efficient unrolling of this -- proceedings and it would allow us to submit all our filings in reasonable time and within a reasonable dead-line. And I just need to mention one more thing: To date we have yet to receive the translation of the judgement into the language of the client, of my client, the accused, and this would be another reason why we would appeal or why we would request for the extension of the number of words in our appeals brief. Your Honour, my apologies, but I've just been told by my assistant that the number of words was not quite precisely recorded in the transcript. So we are requesting an extension of the number of words by 6.000 which would amount to a total of 15.000. And, of course, an extension of time for another 15 days, which would then amount to a total number of 30 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The Prosecution have any comments about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution would not object, Your Honour, to an extension of time, but we would object to an extension of words. Seeing no particular specific reason for such a grand extension of words, of course, a reply is just that, a reply. It is limited only to what is in the response. It's not an opportunity to expand the arguments. As it stands now, the Prosecution can see no particular special reason for such an extension of words. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me get this clear, you want an extension, the number of words, of 6.000, an extra 6.000 words?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In the Sainovic case, which relies on the same factual and legal basis, the Pre-Trial Judge allowed such an increase in terms of the number of words in the reply, from 3.000 up to 9.000 words. In other words, General Lukic, who was a police general, was accorded 9.000 extra words; General Ojdanic, 5.000; and Mr. Sainovic as well as Generals Pavkovic and Lazarevic got 3.000 each. Having in mind that we are alone in these proceedings and that we have to cover all the bases, and also keeping in mind that the Prosecution will most likely use up its fund of 45.000 words in their reply, we believed that this increase by 6.000 words suffices in order for the Defence to do its work properly, in addition to all the other reasons I specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the Trial Chamber, having -- not Trial Chamber, the Appeals Chamber, having heard the submissions and oral motion from the Djordjevic Defence, having also heard the response orally from the Prosecution, decides as follows: In relation to the requested extension of time of 15 days, there being no objection forthcoming from the Prosecution, and because on the face of it the request seems to be justified, the Appeals Chamber accedes to the request and extends the dead-line for the filing of the briefs in reply for both Defence and the Prosecution from the 11th of October to the 26th of October. In relation to the request from the Djordjevic Defence for an additional 6.000 words. Having heard the response of the Prosecution, which essentially objects to such a request, and having considered the particular circumstances of this appeal, the Appeals Chamber acknowledges that an extension of -- a kind of extension would be warranted, albeit not to the extent requested by the Djordjevic Defence, and accordingly grants an extension of 3.000 words to the Defence team, bringing the total now from 9.000 to 12.000. That should be more than sufficient, believe me. Are there any other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Not for the Prosecution, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically when I say there is an extension of 3.000 words, if you want to make use of that facility as well and ask me, I will grant it, too, but I don't think it's the case. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. This concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance and adjourn these proceedings. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
